fan-clutch-assembly.summary: A thermal viscous clutch varies fan speed without making the fan rigidly follow the pump shaft. This reconstruction separates a pump-driven input, output housing, bearing and fluid-control pieces inside a published replacement envelope.
fan-clutch-assembly.limits: One of two catalog nut-size branches is shown. Internal geometry is illustrative; the assembly is sealed and is not a rebuild guide. No slip, temperature, fluid flow or airflow simulation is implemented.

steps.title: Receive pump drive
steps.text: The right-hand threaded nut drives the clutch input shaft. The output housing can rotate at a different speed around its bearing.

steps.title: Sense radiator-exit air
steps.text: The front bimetal spring responds to the air coming through the radiator and operates the internal valve.

steps.title: Meter silicone fluid
steps.text: Opening the valve admits fluid from the reservoir into the working region. More fluid coupling increases fan speed; cooling closes the valve while fluid returns to the reservoir.

steps.title: Transfer torque through shear
steps.text: The illustrated rotor and opposing lands provide a narrow working region. Their clearances are assumptions and do not predict clutch torque.

cooling-fan-assembly.summary: The seven-blade fan comparison uses Dorman's published 18.9-inch diameter and black stamped-steel construction. Four bolts attach its central spider to the clutch output.
cooling-fan-assembly.limits: Exact installed fan identity, blade pitch, stamping contours and rivet details remain unverified. The model does not establish radiator or shroud clearance.

steps.title: Attach the fan to the output
steps.text: The clutch specification gives four threaded holes on a three-inch circle. The fan follows the output housing rather than the input shaft directly.

steps.title: Move air through the radiator
steps.text: Seven blades reproduce the replacement's published count; their illustrative pitch represents a pulling fan. Actual airflow depends on geometry, speed and the surrounding shroud.
